metadata.title: Nvidia initiated, Teradyne downgraded: Wall Street's top analyst calls

content.text:
The most talked about and market moving research calls around Wall Street are now in one place. Here are today's research calls that investors need to know, as compiled by The Fly.
Top 5 Upgrades:
-
Rothschild & Co Redburn upgraded Equifax (EFX) to Buy from Neutral with a price target of $235, up from $214. The company's growth is beginning to benefit from improving execution and delivery on cloud- and AI-driven innovations, the firm tells investors in a research note.
-
Baird upgraded Parsons (PSN) to Outperform from Neutral with a price target of $57, up from $48. Investor sentiment is low and the company's guidance looks conservative, the firm tells investors in a research note.
-
Freedom Broker upgraded Taylor Devices (TAYD) to Buy from Hold with a price target of $70, up from $67, following the fiscal Q4 report. The firm is more positive on the company's medium-term prospects following a "sharp recovery" in its backlog.
-
Morgan Stanley upgraded Ternium (TX) to Overweight from Equal Weight with a price target of $65, up from $55. As tariff negotiations progress among member countries of the USMCA, the firm sees a high probability that the U.S. will reduce import tariffs on Mexican steel, driving price hikes in Mexico's domestic steel prices and benefitting Ternium's profitability.
-
Citi upgraded O-I Glass (OI) to Buy from Neutral with a price target of $9, up from $8, and added an "upside 90-day catalyst watch" on the shares. The firm says the shares are trading at "trough" valuation levels while the company's 2026 outlook is "derisked."
Top 5 Downgrades:
-
Baird downgraded Teradyne (TER) to Neutral from Outperform with an unchanged price target of $420. The firm cites valuation for the downgrade, recommending some profit taking following the stock's recent rally.
-
HSBC downgraded Ternium (TX) to Hold from Buy with a price target of $55, up from $53. The firm says the benefits from price hikes, improving demand and profitability appear mostly priced into Ternium shares.
-
JPMorgan downgraded Limbach (LMB) to Underweight from Neutral with a price target of $50, down from $60. The firm is concerned by the Q2 earnings report, saying the 22% revenue growth was almost entirely acquisition-led, while gross margin compressed.
-
JPMorgan downgraded DoubleVerify (DV) to Neutral from Overweight with a $13.60 price target. The firm cites Nielsen's definitive agreement to acquire DoubleVerify in an all-cash transaction for $13.60 per share for the downgrade.
-
Citi downgraded Weibo (WB) to Neutral from Buy with a price target of $7.80, down from $9.30. The Q2 report was better than expected but the company spoke of challenges for the second half of 2026 and 2027, the firm tells investors in a research note.
